headline: Dollar flat as oil rebounds above $110; hawkish RBA lifts Aussie, peso hits record low
summary: The dollar index was little changed near 101.7 as Brent climbed back above $110 on Gulf shipping risks and the 2-year Treasury yield rose about 2bp to 4.80%, offsetting tech-led stock gains; October Fed hike odds held near 16%. The Aussie led after a hawkish RBA speech, the won hit a fresh two-year high and the rupee a six-week high, while the peso slid to a record 63.361 and the rupiah stayed near 18,000 after Bank Indonesia held.
drivers: Deputy Governor Hauser said the inflation outlook looked materially worse and he was unsure whether another hike is needed, lifting Nov 3 hike odds to about 40%. AUD/USD rose about 0.4% to near 0.7030, the best G10 performer.
Oil and Fed pricing pin the dollar

Brent traded back above $110 after Iran ruled out talks until its demands are met and US stockpiles fell; 2-year yields rose about 2bp to 4.80% while the 10-year held near 5.12%. Futures price only about 16% for an Oct 28 Fed hike but roughly 90% for December, leaving the index stuck near 101.7.
Asia splits on flows and central banks

Chip exports more than doubled in Korea's first 20 days of October and foreigners bought about 660 billion won of shares, taking the won to 1,325.2; Jio IPO inflows lifted the rupee 0.5% to about 94.46. The peso fell 0.43% to a record 63.361 before the BSP, and Bank Indonesia's hold left the rupiah near 18,005.
view: Neutral to mildly weaker into the Fed (Oct 28): October hike odds are low and the index has stalled near 101.7, but Brent above $110 and a December hike that is about 90% priced keep a floor near 101.5. I still fade the dollar against the yen and the Canadian dollar, where central banks lean hawkish, and back it against the rupiah while the MSCI threat stands; I've dropped the Aussie short now that the RBA is talking up another hike. A confirmed Iran deal and lower oil would push the index toward 101; a Fed that signals hikes beyond December would take it back toward 102.5.
ideas: Short from 158.50 is about 0.4 in favour: Himino says underlying inflation is near 2% and Tokyo guards 159–160; hold for 156.80, stop 159.60.
BoC hike odds near 80% for Oct 28; sell bounces into 1.4100–1.4130 for 1.3880, stop 1.4210, about 2.5:1.
BI held its main rate and is adding liquidity while MSCI's threat stands; buy dips toward 17,950–18,000 for 18,250, stop 17,850.
review: No targets or stops hit: the USD/JPY short is about 0.4 in favour, EUR/USD's long about 0.4% up and USD/TWD's fade slightly in favour in late quotes; I close the AUD/USD short near 0.7030 for a small loss (about 0.2%) after the RBA's hawkish turn, USD/INR broke below its 94.50 floor so the range moves lower, and CAD, CHF, KRW and IDR entries were not reached.

eurusd.note: Little changed near 1.1233 as Brent's return above $110 and French bond stress offset a soft dollar.

view.call: Hold longs from 1.1190; ECB December hike is priced.

eurusd.why: The euro's own headwinds did the work. Brent climbed back above $110 after Iran ruled out talks until its demands are met, which hurts an energy importer like the euro area far more than the US, and French bond spreads stayed wide. A 2bp rise in the 2-year Treasury yield to about 4.80% also undid part of Tuesday's dollar dip, leaving the pair near 1.1233 after a 1.1261 high.
eurusd.outlook: I keep the long from 1.1180–1.1190: the ECB is priced to hike in December and the dollar's rate edge has stopped widening, but France and oil cap rallies near 1.1270. A close under 1.1140 would end the call.
eurusd.watch: Euro-area flash consumer confidence (Oct 22) and PMIs (Oct 23), French budget talks, the Fed (Oct 28) and the ECB (Oct 29).

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.1% to near 1.3392; a hot UK CPI print still couldn't break the 1.3410 ceiling.

view.call: 1.3300–1.3450; buy dips, but the Oct 28 Budget caps it.

gbpusd.why: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September against a 3.4% forecast, with core at 2.8% and services at 3.7%, both above estimates, as motor fuel prices jumped almost 30% on the year. Sterling dipped to 1.3364 and recovered, but a Nov 5 BoE hike was already priced at about 90–95%, so the beat confirmed it rather than adding to it, and sellers held 1.3400–1.3410 for a second day.
gbpusd.outlook: Bias is higher while the BoE is set to hike five weeks before the Fed, but the Oct 28 Budget is a real risk, so I keep trading the 1.3300–1.3450 range from the bottom. A daily close above 1.3450 would turn me outright bullish.
gbpusd.watch: UK flash PMIs (Oct 23), the Budget and the Fed (Oct 28) and the BoE (Nov 5).

audusd.note: Led G10, up about 0.4% to near 0.7030 after the RBA's Hauser said the inflation outlook is worse.

view.call: 0.6950–0.7080; RBA hike talk ends the short.

audusd.why: An Australian story. RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook looked materially worse, partly on oil, and that he was unsure whether another hike would be needed next month, lifting the priced chance of a Nov 3 hike to about 40%. Tech-led stock gains and a yuan near its strongest since mid-2022 added support, taking the Aussie to about a three-week high.
audusd.outlook: I close the short near 0.7030: the RBA is no longer clearly on hold, so the policy gap behind the call is narrowing. I'd now trade 0.6950–0.7080 and turn bullish on a close above 0.7080.
audusd.watch: Australia flash PMIs (Oct 23), RBA speakers, yuan fixings and the RBA decision on Nov 3.

usdjpy.note: Flat near 158.13 after a 158.35 Asian high; the 158.50 short is about 0.4 in favour.
usdjpy.why: Two forces cancelled out. Japan's September exports rose 16.7%, missing forecasts, and firmer US 2-year yields near 4.80% helped the dollar early. But BoJ Deputy Governor Himino said underlying inflation is close to 2% and financial conditions remain loose, backing a December hike, and Finance Minister Katayama said she sees no gap with the BoJ, easing worries that the government's tax cuts clash with tightening.
usdjpy.outlook: Asymmetric to the downside: Tokyo and Washington defended 160 jointly in July, swaps price about 80% for a December BoJ hike, and dollar buyers near 159 face intervention risk. Hold the short for 156.80; a close above 159.60 would mean Tokyo tolerates more weakness.
usdjpy.watch: Japan September CPI (Oct 23), the Fed (Oct 28), the BoJ (Oct 30) and warnings from Katayama or Mimura near 159.

usdchf.note: Little changed near 0.8243; the 0.8290 sell zone is still untouched.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 0.8285; the franc trend is intact.

usdchf.why: There was no Swiss driver. The franc tracked the euro, which was held back by oil above $110 and French bond stress, while the dollar drew modest support from higher short-dated Treasury yields. Gulf shipping headlines kept haven demand for the franc steady, and markets still expect the SNB to hold at zero rather than go negative.
usdchf.outlook: The franc trend is intact, so I keep selling bounces toward 0.8280–0.8290 rather than chasing at 0.8243, targeting 0.8180. A close above 0.8360 would end the call.
usdchf.watch: Gulf headlines, European bond spreads, SNB comments and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdcad.note: Steady near 1.4045, close to Tuesday's four-week low of 1.4033; the 1.4100 sell zone wasn't reached.

view.call: Sell bounces into 1.4100–1.4130; BoC hike odds near 80%.

usdcad.why: The loonie held its gains as swaps kept about an 80% chance of a 25bp Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Oct 28, after Governor Macklem said the bank will raise its inflation forecast significantly because of high oil prices. WTI swung between about $97 and $100 with little net change and the dollar index barely moved, so the pair sat near 1.4045 without a fresh catalyst.
usdcad.outlook: I keep selling bounces into 1.4100–1.4130 for the 200-day average near 1.3880; the narrower 2-year yield gap supports the loonie. A close above 1.4210 would end the call; a dovish BoC hold is the main risk.
usdcad.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, and the BoC and Fed decisions on Oct 28.

usdcnh.note: Yuan firm near 6.673 offshore; the PBOC fixed 6.7192, 413 pips weaker than estimates.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 6.69; a slow grind at the PBOC's pace.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC set the midpoint at 6.7192, a touch stronger than Tuesday but 413 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, a clear signal it wants gains slow and steady. It also began daily overnight reverse repos, adding 80 billion yuan, as Governor Pan studies an overnight policy rate. With the dollar flat, the offshore yuan held near 6.673, close to its strongest since mid-2022.
usdcnh.outlook: A managed grind lower in USD/CNH; I'd sell bounces toward 6.69 for 6.64, stop 6.71. An overnight repo rate set below the 1.40% seven-day rate would hint at easing and slow the yuan, while fixes closer to estimates would speed it up.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings versus estimates, the overnight repo rate and US–China trade headlines.

usdhkd.note: Eased to about 7.8464, still close to the 7.85 weak-side limit.

view.call: 7.84–7.85, no trade; an HKMA defence would lift HIBOR fast.

usdhkd.why: USD/HKD stays near the weak edge because Hong Kong interbank rates remain well below US rates, so selling HKD for higher-yielding dollars still pays. Firmer US 2-year yields kept that gap wide, and the slight dip to about 7.8464 came as Asian stocks rebounded rather than from any change in the carry picture.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade. A touch of 7.85 would force the HKMA to buy HKD and lift HIBOR; until then it sits near the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA action at 7.85, the aggregate balance and one-month HIBOR.

usdsgd.note: Flat near 1.2774 as the broad dollar barely moved.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 1.2800; SGD is low-beta.

usdsgd.why: A quiet session. The dollar index barely moved, the yuan held near multi-year highs and Asian stocks rebounded, but oil back above $110 and firmer short-dated US yields offset that support. With the MAS keeping its policy band unchanged on Oct 14 and the S$NEER already near the strong side, the Singapore dollar moves only a fraction as much as its neighbours.
usdsgd.outlook: Mildly lower if the dollar keeps easing into the Fed; I'd sell bounces toward 1.2800 for 1.272, stop 1.285. The Singapore dollar will lag higher-beta Asian currencies in any rally.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore September CPI, the broad dollar and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 2.9 to 1,325.2 at the Seoul close, a two-year high for a fourth straight session.

view.call: Sell rallies into 1,335–1,340; exporters keep selling.

usdkrw.why: Exports and flows both helped. Korea's exports more than doubled to $61.6 billion in the first 20 days of October on record chip shipments, and foreigners turned buyers of about 660 billion won of local shares as the Kospi rebounded 3.3% on easing AI-spending worries. Exporters' dollar sales did the rest, keeping the won at its strongest since early October 2024.
usdkrw.outlook: The trend favours the won, so I still sell rallies into 1,335–1,340 for 1,315 rather than chase it. A renewed foreign exodus on weak AI earnings is the risk; a close above 1,352 would end the call.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign flows in Seoul, Samsung and SK hynix, big-tech earnings this week and Korea's Q3 GDP.

usdtwd.note: Eased to about 32.45 in late quotes after an early 32.655, as foreigners stopped selling Taiwan shares.
usdtwd.why: After ten straight sessions and about NT$838 billion of net selling, foreign investors bought a small NT$0.96 billion of Taiwan shares as the Taiex rose 1.3% on Supermicro's raised AI sales outlook. Futures settlement passed, removing one reason for forced selling, and a record US$23.6 billion September trade surplus backs the currency. The dollar hit 32.655 in the morning before easing; Taipei's closing rate could not be confirmed.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep fading the weakness: outflows have paused, the central bank has said it will act and export receipts are huge. Target 32.10; a close above 32.80 would stop the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign flows on the Taiex, TSMC and US big-tech earnings, and central bank action.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit edged up to 4.0790/4.0825 at the 6pm close on strong local data.
usdmyr.why: Domestic data carried it. September exports jumped 54.5% and third-quarter growth of 5.3% beat forecasts, so some economists now see room for Bank Negara to raise its overnight policy rate. That offset higher oil and firm short-dated US yields; the ringgit gained 0.15 sen against the dollar but slipped against sterling after the UK inflation beat.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Strong exports and talk of Bank Negara tightening support it, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil prices and Bank Negara's Nov 5 meeting.

usdphp.note: Peso fell 27.1 centavos to a record-low close of 63.361 after touching 63.373 before the BSP.

view.call: 63.00–63.50 into the BSP; a soft 25bp hike breaks 63.50.

usdphp.why: Oil back above $110 and Fed hike risk lifted importers' dollar demand, while traders said BSP intervention looked light given falling reserves. A 25bp hike to 5.25% is fully priced (most economists expect it, a couple see 50bp) against September inflation of 7.2%, so the expected move gave no support. The peso is down about 7.2% this year.
usdphp.outlook: I lift the range to 63.00–63.50 into Thursday's decision. A 50bp hike or firm guidance should pull it back toward 63.00; a 25bp hike with soft wording would likely break 63.50, the next resistance traders cite.
usdphp.watch: The BSP decision on Oct 22, oil prices and BSP dollar sales.

usdidr.note: Rupiah slipped about 0.1% to near 18,005 after BI held its main rate; JISDOR firmed to 17,986.

view.call: Buy dips toward 17,950–18,000; MSCI risk, BI held.

usdidr.why: Bank Indonesia held its benchmark at 5.75%, disappointing the 14 of 29 economists who expected a hike, but raised the deposit facility rate 25bp to 5.00% and sweetened DNDF hedging incentives. It also cut reserve requirements in two steps, releasing about 190 trillion rupiah of liquidity. The mixed package left the rupiah slightly weaker, with MSCI's standalone threat still weighing on foreign flows.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long the dollar on dips toward 17,950–18,000 while the MSCI threat stands and BI adds liquidity, targeting 18,250. A credible government fix for MSCI that pulls it below 17,850 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Foreign flows into Jakarta stocks, the government's response to MSCI, bond auctions and BI intervention.

usdinr.note: Rupee jumped about 0.5% to near 94.46, a six-week high, on Jio IPO inflows and RBI curbs.
usdinr.why: Foreign investors sold dollars to subscribe to Reliance's roughly 302 billion rupee Jio Platforms IPO, which opened on Wednesday, and RBI measures limiting oil companies' spot dollar buying kept demand in check. The rupee reached about 94.35–94.41 intraday, its best since early September, before Brent near $111 and weak local stocks capped the gain.
usdinr.outlook: The range moves lower to 94.00–95.00: IPO flows support the rupee near term, but oil above $110 and the RBI's preference for stability limit a rally. I wouldn't chase it either way.
usdinr.watch: Jio IPO subscription flows, oil and Iran headlines, RBI action and foreign portfolio flows.

eurjpy.note: Little changed near 177.6 as both the euro and yen held flat against the dollar.

view.call: 176–179; the BoJ on Oct 30 is the event risk.

eurjpy.why: Neither leg moved much. The euro was capped by oil above $110 and French bond stress, while the yen drew support from BoJ Deputy Governor Himino's hawkish remarks but lost a little on soft export data. With EUR/USD near 1.1233 and USD/JPY near 158.13, the cross settled around 177.6.
eurjpy.outlook: Range 176–179. The ECB (Oct 29) and BoJ (Oct 30) meet back to back; a hawkish BoJ would break it lower, while a French budget deal would lift it.
eurjpy.watch: French bond spreads, Japan CPI on Oct 23, and the ECB and BoJ meetings.

cnhjpy.note: Near 23.70, at the top of its range, with the yuan and yen both steady.
cnhjpy.why: The PBOC kept braking the yuan with a fix far weaker than estimates, while the yen held near 158 per dollar, so CNH/JPY stayed near 23.70 (USD/JPY near 158.13 divided by USD/CNH near 6.673), close to the top of its recent range.
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range: the PBOC slows yuan gains while Tokyo guards the yen's weak side. A break above 23.8 would need the yen to weaken through 159.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, the overnight repo rate and Japanese intervention signals.

watch: Next: the BSP (Oct 22), Japan CPI and flash PMIs (Oct 23), the Fed, BoC and UK Budget (Oct 28), the ECB and BoJ (Oct 29–30), the RBA (Nov 3) and BoE (Nov 5), Gulf headlines and oil, and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
